reason: Epigeous stems and stolons grow above the ground, which is the meaning of FLOPO:0991036 aerial; the opposite word 'souterraines' already maps to FLOPO:0991035 subterranean. 'Germination epigeous' is about how a seedling comes up, not about where a part sits, so the rule should not apply to seed statements.

A glomerule is a dense, head-like cluster of nearly stalkless flowers on a very short axis, which matches the definition of FLOPO:0991006 capitate. PO lists glomerule as a synonym of compound capitulum (PO_0030122), but floras use the word in a different sense (Amaranthaceae, Urticaceae, sedges), so a bearer rule would be wrong.
An adverb that says how fast a change happens ('gradually narrowed', 'gradually reduced'). It is not a quality on its own; the quality is the word it modifies.

target: docs/flora-annotation-playbook.md (compound shape 'X-Y' as a continuum: linear PATO_0001199 – ovate FLOPO:0991024)
reason: A compound of two shapes that both have terms. The existing compound-shape rule reads 'X-Y' as a value between the two.
'Straight' already has a term (PATO_0002180) and 'nearly' marks an approximate value, as '±' does.

target: comparison or relation stated without its second term
reason: 'Distal leaves not reduced' means not smaller than the other leaves. That is a comparison whose second term is missing, so it is rejected like 'smaller' and 'shorter' in the previous review.

'Ray florets' and 'ray flowers' are the PO class ray flower (synonym ray floret), and 'ray corolla' is the corolla of a ray flower (pattern 12). 'Trichomes rays' (the arms of star-shaped hairs) is a different sense, so the rule should not apply to trichomes.

label: segmentiform
definition: A 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being shaped like a segment of an orange: a wedge with a convex outer face and two flat inner faces meeting along an inner edge. NOTE: Used for seeds and mericarps that fill one sector of a rounded fruit.
reason: A real botanical shape of seeds and mericarps that has no PATO or FLOPO term. Compounds such as 'compressed-segmentiform' are then handled as continua.
Exstipulate means without stipules. It is the opposite of the existing rule for 'stipulate' (C210).

'Leaflets of decreasing size' describes a series whose size gets smaller along its length, which is PATO_0005015 tapered size (synonym 'gradient of size'). Apply it only when size is meant; 'decreasing hairiness' and the bare word 'decreasing' should stay unmapped.
This is a fragment of 'divided almost to the base', which means deeply split. PATO_0001786 split is the closest existing term. The depth of the cut is lost, but adding a new term would be doubtful.
Scutelliform means shaped like a small dish or platter, which is round and shallowly concave as in FLOPO:0991182 saucer-shaped. It is not peltate, which is about where a stalk is attached.

target: docs/flora-annotation-playbook.md (compound 'X-Y' as a continuum: subulate PATO_0001954 – acuminate PATO_0002228)
reason: A compound of two values that both have terms. It goes through the existing compound reading and needs no new term.

target: docs/flora-annotation-playbook.md (compound 'X-Y' as a continuum: lanate PATO_0104357 – tomentose PATO_0002341)
reason: A compound of two hair-cover values that both have terms (woolly is a synonym of lanate).

label: close-grained
definition: A texture quality inhering in wood by virtue of its having narrow growth rings and small, closely packed cells and vessels, so that its surface is fine and even. NOTE: Wood anatomy; the opposite is coarse-grained.
reason: A standard wood quality with no PATO or FLOPO term. PATO_0001164 dense is too broad, and floras state density separately ('strong, dense, and close-grained').

label: semi-sagittate
definition: An arrow-shaped quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's having a backward-pointing basal lobe on one side only, like one half of an arrowhead. NOTE: Child of PATO:0001881 arrow-shaped; used for stipules.
reason: A distinct, recurring stipule shape that the parent arrow-shaped would misstate, because the parent has two basal lobes. It is modelled like obtriangular under triangular.
'Flowers without spathe' says that a spathe is absent. The FLOPO class spathe already exists.
This is a plain negation of PATO_0002112 perforate (having a hole or holes), said of moss leaf cells and seed condyles.
A loose likeness with no fixed meaning: finely divided, pinnate, or the look of fern veins. The real content ('pinnate') is stated in the same sentence and is annotated from there.

'Multilocular' gives the number of locules (the chambers of an ovary, fruit or anther) as 'many', which is a count pattern like 'N-locular'. Examples such as 'up to 25 locular' carry the number. Anther 'multilocellées' counts anther locules (PO_0025264).
This is the negation of the existing FLOPO value class anastomosing, which applies to veins.
'Closely set' means close to the nearest parts of the same kind without being joined to them, which is exactly FLOPO:0991190 approximate, the opposite of distant.
An adjective that picks out which part is meant (floral bract, floral bud, floral stem), not a quality. It belongs to identifying the part (bearer rules or pattern 12).

target: docs/flora-annotation-playbook.md (compound 'X-Y' as a continuum: ovate FLOPO:0991024 – triangular PATO_0001875)
reason: A compound of two shapes that both have terms (deltate maps to triangular under rule C226).
This is a plain negation of PATO_0001810 wrinkled.
This negates PATO_0001373 glistening (synonyms glossy, shiny). The negation is closer to the text than FLOPO:0991106 dull, which says more than the source does.
'Without spots' negates PATO_0000333 spotted. The previous review rejected 'spot' as a part, so an absence rule does not fit.

target: docs/odp/09-relation-to-another-part.md (width of the base, plant organ base FLOPO_0985024, towards the apex FLOPO_0985023)
reason: A comparison between two regions of the same part ('wider at the base than the tip'). It needs the relation pattern with the base as the part of the bearer, not a new term.

target: comparison or relation stated without its second term
reason: A density comparison without what it is compared with, like 'denser' (C365).
'Semi-' here works like 'sub-' and '±': a value close to prostrate, the same way 'semi-erect' sits next to erect. It needs no new term.
